generator.description: Published local circumstances of three lunar occultations, transcribed from the pages named below and retrieved 2026-09-25. Times only (facts); nothing else is reproduced. Never regenerated from Rust output (CONVENTIONS section 11).
generator.places: None of the sources states the coordinates it used for a city; each place here is the city's usual centre (or the Royal Observatory for Greenwich), so a few kilometres of difference in the observing point are part of each tolerance.
generator.tolerance: Rounding of the published time (30 s for whole minutes, 3 s for tenths of a minute, 0.5 s for seconds) plus 60 s for the unstated observing point and the prediction's limb and ephemeris; a chord that meets the limb obliquely moves fastest with position.

events.source: Michael E. Bakich, 'Watch the full Moon cover Mars', Astronomy (astronomy.com/observing/watch-the-full-moon-cover-mars/); Jeffrey L. Hunt, 'Wolf Moon occults Mars' (whenthecurveslineup.com/2024/12/30/2025-january-13-wolf-moon-occults-mars/); both from IOTA's prediction
events.published_as: local clock times, whole minutes (EST = UTC-5, CST = UTC-6)

events.source: Mike Foulkes, 'Observers' challenge: a lunar occultation of Saturn on 2024 August 21', British Astronomical Association (britastro.org/2024/observers-challenge-a-lunar-occultation-of-saturn-on-2024-august-21)
events.published_as: UT to a tenth of a minute

events.source: Bruce McClure, 'Moon occults Aldebaran on December 30', EarthSky (earthsky.org/sky-archive/moon-occults-aldebaran-on-december-30/), from IOTA's prediction
events.published_as: UT to the second (London GMT and Reykjavik UTC in December)
